title: A good intention counts
hook: a sacred hadith: whoever intends a good and doesn't do it, one good is written; whoever does it, ten or more
tomorrow: the duties, or the extras: which one brings you closer?

segments.voice: Yesterday, relieve a distress: the merchant who let the debt go, and help that runs alongside you while you help. Help, and be helped. Today, the help you meant to give.
screen: `HELP, AND BE HELPED.` → `THE HELP YOU MEANT TO GIVE.`

segments.voice: A week of plans that never happened: the call to an aunt, the form half filled in, the visit pushed to next time. Yesterday's question: you meant to do a good thing and never did; does it count at all? Hadith thirty-seven is a sacred hadith, words the Prophet, peace be upon him, gives from Allah, reported by Ibn Abbas. And it says yes: whoever intends a good deed and doesn't do it, one full good deed is written. Then it gets stranger.
screen: `PLANS THAT NEVER HAPPENED.` → `A SACRED HADITH.` → `THEN IT GETS STRANGER.`

segments.voice: Here's the whole ledger, in paraphrase from Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim. Intend a good and don't do it: one good deed, written in full. Intend a good and do it: ten good deeds, up to seven hundred times, and beyond, to many multiples. Intend a bad deed and don't do it: one full good deed. Intend a bad deed and do it: one bad deed, just one. There's the puzzle. Why would a wrong you never did earn you a good deed? Muslim's wording solves it: because he left it for My sake. Not doing it wasn't an empty space. Turning away was a choice, and a choice is a deed. So the scale is tilted on purpose. Goods multiply, wrongs stay single, and even a stopped wrong becomes a good. The Qur'an says the first part too, in Pickthall's words: "Whoso bringeth a good deed will receive tenfold the like thereof." Here's the line to tell a friend tonight: in this ledger, the moment you stop yourself counts as a good thing you did.
screen: `INTEND A GOOD: ONE IS WRITTEN.` · `DO IT: TEN, AND BEYOND.` · `A STOPPED WRONG BECOMES A GOOD.` · `THE SCALE IS TILTED ON PURPOSE.` · then, large: `INTENDING COUNTS.`

segments.voice: On a scrap of paper, write by hand three small goods you mean to do tomorrow: a call, a dish washed, a kind word to someone specific. Keep them small enough to be real. For the sit, rest your hand on the list; by this hadith, the meaning is already written.
screen: `THREE SMALL GOODS, BY HAND.` · `THE MEANING IS ALREADY WRITTEN.`

segments.voice: A good intention counts: meant and not done, one good deed is written; meant and done, ten and beyond. And a wrong you turn from becomes a good.
Pocket this: intending counts, and the doing of it counts many times over. That's hadith thirty-seven.

howItsDone: Muslims often make an intention for a good deed before they're able to do it, trusting this hadith that the intention itself is written, and teachers use it to encourage turning away from a wrong for Allah's sake.

fork.setup: you're about to snap at your sister, and you stop yourself, for God's sake. by hadith thirty-seven, what's written for that moment?
options: nothing: nothing happened, so nothing's written.
a bad deed, because you meant to snap.
a full good deed, for leaving it.
fork.reveal: in Muslim's wording, he left it for My sake, so one full good deed is written. turning away is a deed.

original.note: Arabic: he intended a good deed. hasanah is a good deed; hamma means he set his mind on it.

trapdoor: what you thought: it's the thought that counts, more or less.
what it means: a good intended is written; a good done multiplies; a wrong left for Allah becomes a good.
what a scholar hears: a hadith qudsi in Bukhari 6491 and Muslim 131, with 'he left it for My sake' in Muslim's wording, and Qur'an 6:160 on tenfold.

chat.says: meant to drive Dadi to her checkup but the car died. so that good deed just... doesn't count?
options: It was written when you meant it. Now do the next good you can, like calling her.
It counts the same as doing it, so you're all done. No need to follow up at all.
Only finished deeds count. Meaning well without doing it is basically just a wish.
chat.meaning: A good intended is written in full, and a good done counts many times over. So the intention counts, and the next good is still worth doing.

Ibn Abbas.meaning: the Prophet's young cousin, who reported this hadith

sacred hadith.meaning: words the Prophet gives from Allah, outside the Qur'an

Sahih al-Bukhari.meaning: a major hadith collection, compiled by Imam al-Bukhari

Pickthall.meaning: an English translator of the Qur'an whose words are quoted here
